title.rendered: Blessed Are Those Who Hunger for Righteousness: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied.” A morning devotional on the holy appetite God delights to fill.

content.rendered:
Hunger is not a mood. Thirst is not a preference. They are bodily commands. Ignore them long enough and the body dies. Jesus takes those two most primal drives of the human body and applies them to the soul.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, August 31, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, For they shall be filled.”
Matthew 5:6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Hunger is not a mood. Thirst is not a preference. They are bodily commands. When the body needs food, hunger sends signals the mind cannot easily override. When the body needs water, thirst rises so insistently that a person who has gone without water for even a day can think of almost nothing else. Ignore hunger and thirst long enough, and the body dies. They are two of the most primal, undeniable, insistent drives in the human experience. And Jesus takes those two drives and, in the fourth beatitude, applies them to the human soul.

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.” He is not talking about a mild spiritual interest. He is not talking about the person who reads a Christian book now and again and prays occasionally when things are hard. Jesus is describing the person whose appetite for the righteousness of God is as insistent, as undeniable, as bodily-real as physical hunger and thirst. The person who cannot go a day without seeking Him. The person who feels the ache of separation when the soul goes without His presence for too long. That kind of hunger, Jesus says, is blessed. And it is the one hunger God has committed Himself to fill.

The Passion Translation captures the beauty of the beatitude: “How enriched you are when you crave righteousness! For you will be surrounded with fruitfulness” (Matthew 5:6 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Blessed and fortunate and happy and spiritually prosperous (in that state in which the born-again child of God enjoys His favor and salvation) are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness (uprightness and right standing with God), for they shall be completely satisfied!” (Matthew 5:6 AMPC). Completely satisfied. The Greek verb Jesus uses for “filled” here is chortazō. It was originally used of livestock at feeding time. Filled to the point of complete satisfaction. Filled until the appetite is stilled. That is what God does with the soul that genuinely hungers for Him.

The beatitude carries a quiet judgment on every substitute appetite the human heart has ever chased. Career success will not satisfy the soul. Relationships will not satisfy the soul. Money will not satisfy the soul. Fame will not satisfy the soul. Even good gifts of God, when made ultimate, will leave the soul still hungry. The one appetite God has committed to satisfy fully, permanently, and personally is the appetite for Himself and for the righteousness that is found only in Christ. Every other hunger will leave the soul reaching for the next thing. This one hunger, God fills to the brim.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, examine your appetites. What are you hungering for this week? What are you thirsting for? If the answer is anything less than God Himself, the fill will not last. But if the answer is Him, if there is even a small hunger for His presence, His word, His righteousness, take courage. That hunger is blessed. And the promise attached to it is not a maybe. Not a possibly. Not a we will see. You shall be filled. Completely. Satisfied. Bring the hunger to Him today, and He will meet it with Himself.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that the deepest appetite of my soul is for You. Every other appetite I have chased has left me still reaching for the next thing. Only You satisfy. Today I bring You the hunger. I bring You the thirst. I stop trying to fill the God-shaped ache with career, relationships, success, or approval. I come to You directly. Fill me with Yourself. Fill me with the righteousness of Christ. Fill me until the appetite is stilled. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I hunger and thirst for the righteousness of God. He has promised to fill me completely. My deepest appetite is for Him, and He satisfies it in Christ today.
